title: Power Apps: prompt columns can store multiple lines of text output
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly reports that automation for the environment's AI prompts setting is not documented. Microsoft documents a writable Dataverse organization property for that setting; the roadmap facts, UI controls and general prompt-column licensing are supported.

claims.claim: How a maker chooses multi-line prompt-column output is not yet documented.

claims.claim: No source states whether the multi-line change alters existing prompt columns.

claims.claim: A stored multi-line prompt-output length limit is not yet documented.

claims.claim: No licensing provision specific to multi-line output is published.

claims.claim: A prompt column is a Dataverse data type for natural-language prompts tied to other columns.
claims.quote: A prompt column is an AI-powered data type in Microsoft Dataverse that enables you to define natural language prompts tied to other columns in your table.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Prompt columns persist their generative AI results in the table.
claims.quote: The key function is that the prompt column contains generative AI results stored in the table persistently.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Creating a record triggers the prompt.
claims.quote: A prompt executes when you create a record or update one or more of the columns that the prompt references.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Updating one or more referenced columns triggers the prompt.
claims.quote: A prompt executes when you create a record or update one or more of the columns that the prompt references.

claims.claim: Learn says on-demand prompt-column execution without updating a record is not currently supported.
claims.quote: Can I perform on-demand AI analysis without updating a record? Prompt columns are triggered automatically on record updates; however, on-demand execution is not currently supported.

claims.claim: Insufficient permission on an input column is a documented cause of generation failure.
claims.quote: The user doesn't have sufficient permissions on one or more input columns referenced in the prompt column definition.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Prompt columns are not audited.
claims.quote: Are prompt columns audited? Prompt columns aren't audited.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Each prompt column has corresponding Status and Details columns created automatically.
claims.quote: When a prompt column is created, the table automatically includes two corresponding columns, Status and Details, for that prompt column.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Status and Details columns record execution status and failure details.
claims.quote: When prompt execution starts, these columns are populated to record the execution status and any failure details.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises human review before generated content informs a business decision.
claims.quote: A human should review the content before you post it online, send it to a customer, or use it to inform a business decision.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Prompt columns use the same licensing model as AI Builder prompts.
claims.quote: Prompt columns use the same licensing model as AI builder prompts.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; cost; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Consumption is the licensing model, with variable metered cost in AI Builder credits or Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Prompt columns consume credits every time a prompt is executed. Copilot Credits are a common currency for eligible Microsoft services with usage-based billing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The prompts overview lists Copilot Credits as a prerequisite.
claims.quote: You need Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: The prompts overview requires Dataverse installed in the environment.
claims.quote: Microsoft Dataverse is installed on the environment.

claims.claim: The prompts overview requires an environment in an available region.
claims.quote: Your environment is in the list of available regions.

claims.claim: Prompt columns support AI Builder credits and Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Prompt columns consume both AI Builder credits and Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: The prompt-columns article says AI Builder credits are retiring soon.
claims.quote: AI Builder credits are retiring soon.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: AI Builder features in apps and flows first try AI Builder credits, then Copilot Credits when absent or exhausted.
claims.quote: AI Builder features in apps and flows first try to consume AI Builder credits, then if absent or exhausted, they try to consume Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Prompt runs consume AI credit capacity available to the environment.
claims.quote: Once an environment has Copilot Credits available, it can run the AI Builder features in all contexts. If an environment only has AI Builder credits available, it can only run AI Builder features in Power Apps and Power Automate.

claims.claim: Credits are consumed every time a prompt column executes its prompt.
claims.quote: Prompt columns consume credits every time a prompt is executed.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Testing a prompt in the designer is free.
claims.quote: In the prompt designer, select Test. ... Testing a prompt is free. The credits on lower right are estimates for one run.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls: monitoring
claims.claim: The prompt-column credit report is at Power Automate > Automation center > AI Builder activity.
claims.quote: Sign in to Power Automate. On the left navigation pane, select Automation center, and then select AI Builder activity.

claims.claim: The report's Estimated consumption column shows credits consumed per prompt execution.
claims.quote: Review the Estimated consumption column to see the credits consumed by each prompt execution.

claims.claim: Prompt-column filter conditions reduce unnecessary executions and help optimise credit consumption.
claims.quote: During record creation or update, the prompt column evaluates the filter first and then executes the prompt for eligible records. This approach reduces unnecessary executions and helps optimize Copilot credit consumption.

claims.claim: Prompt-run cost depends on input tokens, output tokens and model version, so longer output can increase consumption.
claims.quote: Output tokens refer to the tokens generated by the model in its response. ... The combination of input tokens, output tokens, and the model version allows you to compute the cost of your prompt run.

claims.claim: The prompt-columns prerequisites require the environment's Copilot feature to be on.
claims.quote: Copilot and AI Prompts features turned On in the Features area for the environment settings.

claims.claim: The prompt-columns prerequisites require the environment's AI Prompts feature to be on.
claims.quote: Copilot and AI Prompts features turned On in the Features area for the environment settings.

claims.claim: A table can have up to five prompt columns.
claims.quote: You can create up to five prompt columns per table.

claims.claim: Block unmanaged customizations must be disabled to create or edit prompt columns.
claims.quote: To create or edit Prompt Columns, the 'Block unmanaged customizations' environment setting must be disabled.

claims.claim: The general AI prompts feature is enabled by default.
claims.quote: By default, the AI prompts feature is enabled for makers to create and experiment with various AI-generated content.

claims.claim: Changing environment feature settings requires System Administrator or equivalent permissions.
claims.quote: Ensure you have the System Administrator security role or equivalent permissions to update the settings.

claims.claim: The environment control is in Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > AI Builder > AI prompts.
claims.quote: Select Environments > [select an environment] > Settings > Product > Features. ... On the Features settings page under AI Builder, enable or disable the AI prompts toggle.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The environment AI prompts setting governs whether prompt columns can execute.
claims.quote: Why didn't the prompt column execute? ... AI Prompt feature is disabled.

claims.claim: An AI prompts environment-group rule can govern the same feature for grouped environments.
claims.quote: If your environment is part of an environment group, you can also govern AI prompts feature availability through the AI prompts environment group rule.

claims.claim: Publishing an AI prompts group rule locks the environment setting, which must then be changed through the group rule.
claims.quote: If an environment group rule governing AI prompts is published, it locks the AI prompts setting at the environment-level ... To change the setting, admins must modify the corresponding rule in the environment group that includes the environment.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first row; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an API or command for the environment AI prompts setting.
claims.quote: Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations. Operations supported: GET PATCH. aipromptsenabled | Edm.Boolean | Indicates whether AI Prompts feature is enabled. Display name: Enable AI Prompts.
claims.fix: Replace controls[0].api null with kind 'rest', call 'PATCH /api/data/v9.2/organizations(<organizationid>)', and docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/reference/organization?view=dataverse-latest'. Add to that row's note: 'The request body sets aipromptsenabled to true or false.' Update the rendered API cell to match and remove only the AI prompts setting from the API open question, leaving the column-level setting open. The Organization entity/table references document this Boolean as writable; the Web API update procedure at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/update-delete-table-rows documents PATCH with the properties to update.

claims.claim: The maker control is at Power Apps > Tables > table > Columns > column > Edit column > Allow prompt column execution.
claims.quote: Select Tables on the left navigation pane. Open the table, select Columns, and then open the column that is of data type Prompt ... On the Edit column pane, clear the Allow prompt column execution checkbox.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; controls[1].note; Governance guidance: At rollout; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Clearing Allow prompt column execution disables AI analysis for that individual column.
claims.quote: When disabled, AI analysis isn't performed for the prompt column.

claims.claim: Allow prompt column execution is enabled by default.
claims.quote: By default, the Allow prompt column execution setting is enabled.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: second row; Open questions
claims.claim: No API or command is documented for the per-column Allow prompt column execution setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Allow prompt column execution" API PowerShell; "prompt column" "execution" "Web API"; "prompt column" "IsEnabled". Opened Learn prompt-column and Dataverse msdyn_aiconfiguration Web API reference; no property or operation for this switch was documented.

claims.claim: Learn says both tenant-level and column-level settings must be enabled for prompts to execute.
claims.quote: For prompts to be executed, both tenant level and column level settings need to be enabled.

claims.claim: The corresponding prompt-column Status and Details columns can be added to the table's displayed columns to monitor execution.
claims.quote: Search and select the columns named: (columnName) _PromptColumnStatus; (columnName)_PromptColumnDetails. Select Save. Select Edit to the right of the list to open the columns list with records in a separate view.
